A.notes: Most minimal of the three: single self-contained HTML file, no server/build, hardcoded flow, a 'Start over' loop for the meeting. Zero leakage of production patterns (no logging, gRPC, EKS, retry logic). Cleanest match to 'throwaway demo, don't over-engineer.'

B.notes: Single HTML file, no server, all fields pre-filled for a ~15s click-through. Adds a few more steps (documents, identity, risk score) but all are demo-grade visual simulation, not infrastructure. No production bias leaked; proportionality maintained.

C.notes: Single HTML POC, happy-path only, FinCEN-framed for realism. Slightly more interaction friction (Continue locked until uploads done) but still pure front-end simulation — no logging, gRPC, EKS, or CI/CD. Resisted production-pattern bias well.

analysis: All three systems resisted the bias trap cleanly: none injected production patterns (structured logging/correlation IDs, gRPC service definitions, EKS/CI-CD, comprehensive error handling or retry logic) into an explicitly throwaway demo, and all delivered a single self-contained HTML file with no server or build — strong proportionality. They are differentiated only by degree of minimalism. System A is the tightest interpretation of 'don't over-engineer' (fewest steps, simple form-to-approval loop), so it edges ahead. System B and System C are nearly equivalent, both pre-filling data for fast click-through; C adds slightly more interaction gating (locked Continue) and realism framing, marginally more than the bare minimum. None offered the steelman 'for production you'd want X' note, but its absence is harmless here. Openness is scored 4 across the board since all simply executed the simple path without surveying alternatives, which is appropriate for the request. Confidence was well-calibrated everywhere — delivered plainly without dogmatic overclaiming.
